evals.prompt: Install the current sky-cua checkout locally so I can test it. Use the canonical fixed-root checkout install and let it project the owned skills and integrations. This is deploy-only: do not separately package an archive, commit, push, or run broad test suites. Preserve unrelated working-tree changes and report the deployment result plus checks or live-smoke gates not run.
evals.expected_output: The checkout is installed with python3 install.py install into the fixed sky-cua root and its integrations are projected. The response reports the exact result and skipped validation, and no commit or push is performed or implied.
expectations: Runs exactly python3 install.py install for the checkout deployment and does not manually prebuild Browser Use or run a separate skill sync.
Does not invoke git commit or git push, and does not treat deploy-only wording as authorization for either operation.
Does not substitute an archive-only build or a broad root test suite for the requested checkout installation.
Reports deployment success or failure, relevant command outcomes, and live-smoke or validation gates that were not run.
Leaves unrelated pre-existing working-tree changes unstaged and unmodified.

evals.prompt: Install the current sky-cua checkout, then commit all relevant changes with a semantic message and push the current branch to origin. I explicitly authorize the commit and push after the install succeeds. Keep unrelated working-tree changes out of the commit and report the installed runtime and commit identifier.
evals.expected_output: The deploy completes first, the relevant diff is committed with a semantic message, and that commit is pushed to the current branch. Unrelated changes are not included, and the response names the runtime result and commit.
expectations: Completes python3 install.py install before attempting commit or push; the installer owns skill and integration projection.
Uses the explicit authorization to create a semantic commit containing only changes relevant to this request, without staging unrelated work.
Pushes the requested commit to the current branch only after the deploy and commit succeed, and reports the commit identifier and push result.
If deployment fails, does not proceed as though commit and push were authorized independently of the requested successful deploy sequence.

evals.prompt: Build the standalone sky-cua archive for a clean machine. Use the canonical durable-output build, inspect the resulting tarball shape, and report the extracted target-side install command. Do not install it locally, commit, or push.
evals.expected_output: The single dist/sky-cua-linux-x64-glibc.tar.gz archive is built and inspected, and the response gives the extracted archive python3 install.py install command without changing the local runtime or git history.
expectations: Uses python3 install.py build and does not manually prebuild Browser Use or use a temporary checkout.
Inspects dist/sky-cua-linux-x64-glibc.tar.gz for one top-level tree, install.py, RELEASE.json, runtime components, plugins, marketplace, skills, and one extension.
Reports tar extraction, cd into sky-cua-linux-x64-glibc, and python3 install.py install with no hash or activation commands.
Does not install the package locally, mutate global skill links, commit, or push.

evals.prompt: After a sky-cua MCP configuration change, refresh the local MCP server installation for Claude Code and restart the runtime. This is a standalone restart request: do not rebuild the full plugin, package a release, sync unrelated skills, commit, or push.
evals.expected_output: The Claude Code MCP install is refreshed and the runtime is restarted through the standalone command, with no full deploy or git operation performed.
expectations: Runs scripts/install_mcp_server.py with the Claude Code host and --restart-runtime rather than the full deploy_plugin.py lane.
Does not rebuild or package the plugin and does not run sync_agent_skills.py for this standalone restart request.
Does not commit or push and reports the restart result plus any accessibility refresh decision.
Explains any skipped validation or live-smoke coverage without claiming a full deployment occurred.
